student_metadata.course: CS 5010 - Analytics & Systems of Big Data Practice

currency_parsing.methodology: Regex and string parser stripping '€', multiplying 'M' suffixes by 1,000,000, 'K' suffixes by 1,000, converting to float64.

ratings_and_hits.ratings_treatment: Stripped '★' star glyphs and cast to discrete integer ratings (1 to 5).
ratings_and_hits.hits_treatment: Parsed numeric strings and converted 'K' multipliers to absolute numeric floats.

contract_and_joined.treatment: Extracted year values from joined date strings, parsed contract ranges ('YYYY ~ YYYY'), handled loans and free transfers.

fig1_doughnut_tiers.plot_type: Doughnut Chart with Percentage Callouts & Center Stat
fig1_doughnut_tiers.key_inferences: Overall player ratings (OVA) follow a right-skewed normal distribution. Only 0.6% (109 players) achieve the 'Elite (85+)' tier, while the vast majority reside in 'Mid (65-74)' (50.2%, 8,592 players) and 'Developing (<65)' (36.0%, 6,164 players). High-tier players (75-84) account for 13.2% (2,260 players), establishing high selectivity for world-class status.

fig2_pareto_nationalities.plot_type: Pareto Chart (Dual Axis: Valuation Bars + Cumulative Line)
fig2_pareto_nationalities.key_inferences: Validates the Pareto 80/20 principle in sports economics. The top 5 footballing nations (Spain, England, France, Brazil, Germany) generate over 47.8% of global player valuation. The top 14 nations account for over 75% of cumulative market valuation, demonstrating immense geographic concentration of top-tier talent in Western Europe and South America.

fig3_radar_positions.plot_type: Radar / Spider Polygon Chart (6 Radial Axes)
fig3_radar_positions.key_inferences: Distinct morphological profiles emerge across tactical roles: Forwards dominate in Pace (70.8) and Shooting (65.7) but lag in Defending (31.8); Midfielders exhibit the most balanced polyvalent profile with high Passing (63.9), Dribbling (68.2), and Pace (69.8); Defenders peak in Physicality (69.0) and Defending (65.3); Goalkeepers show specialized distribution reflecting bespoke goalkeeping attributes.

fig4_area_wage_age.plot_type: Area Chart with Dual Axis (Progression & Cumulative)
fig4_area_wage_age.key_inferences: Weekly wage expenditure exhibits an inverted U-curve peaking at Age 28 (€17.67M/week). Over 65% of the total global wage bill is commanded by players between ages 23 and 29 ('Peak Years'). The cumulative expenditure reaches its 50% milestone at Age 26.5, showing that clubs invest disproportionately in prime-age experience.

fig5_correlation_heatmap.key_inferences: Market Value and Wage exhibit strong positive linear correlations with Overall Rating (r = 0.63 and r = 0.58). Among technical traits, Reactions (r = 0.87 with OVA), Composure (r = 0.71 with OVA), and Short Passing (r = 0.50 with OVA) are the primary determinants of elite rating. Dribbling and Finishing correlate heavily with attacking positions.

fig6_violin_value_positions.plot_type: Violin Plot with Embedded Interquartile Boxplot
fig6_violin_value_positions.key_inferences: Attacking positions (Central Forwards CF, Strikers ST, and Left/Right Wingers LW/RW) command substantial valuation premiums with fatter upper density tails on the log valuation scale. Defensive positions (Fullbacks LB/RB, Centre Backs CB, and Goalkeepers GK) have lower median valuations and compressed spreads, highlighting market bias toward goal-scorers.

fig7_scatter_age_growth.plot_type: Scatter Plot with 3rd-Degree Polynomial Regression & Potential Envelope
fig7_scatter_age_growth.key_inferences: The polynomial regression curve shows rapid rating ascension from age 16 to 24, peaking at age ~28.2 (mean OVA ~71.4), followed by a gradual post-32 decline. The shaded potential envelope illustrates significant development headroom for teenagers (up to +18 OVA growth), which diminishes to near zero beyond age 27.

fig8_treemap_clubs.plot_type: Hierarchical Treemap Sized by Squad Market Value
fig8_treemap_clubs.key_inferences: A high concentration of elite valuation exists among top European super-clubs: Liverpool (€852.9M), Real Madrid (€765.7M), Manchester City (€752.8M), and FC Barcelona (€714.1M) lead the valuation hierarchy. The English Premier League and Spanish La Liga dominate the top 20 spaces, illustrating extreme financial disparity in European football.

fig9_hexbin_speed_agility.key_inferences: Sprint Speed and Agility share a robust positive correlation (r = 0.76). The highest density cluster (hexbin mode) sits at (65-72 Speed, 64-70 Agility). The upper-right quadrant isolates elite speedsters (wingers/forwards), while tall central defenders and goalkeepers cluster in the lower-left biomechanical quadrant (<50 Speed, <50 Agility).

fig10_hist_kde_skewness.plot_type: Two-Panel Histogram with Gaussian KDE Overlay
fig10_hist_kde_skewness.key_inferences: Demonstrates successful variance stabilization and skewness reduction. Raw player market valuation is heavily right-skewed (Skewness = +6.27, Kurtosis = +53.84) with severe multi-million euro positive outliers. Applying logarithmic transformation Log_Value = ln(1 + Value) stabilizes variance, transforming active player valuation into a near-symmetric Gaussian distribution (Skewness = +0.35, Kurtosis = -0.08), satisfying core linear modeling assumptions.
